children: Indonesian retail sales rose 1.1% in July from a year ago, after a run of monthly contractions since April, a survey released by the central bank showed on Thursday.
Below are the details from the survey:
Bank Indonesia (BI) said the rise in July was driven by higher purchases of food, beverages, tobacco and spare parts.

However, BI predicted that retail sales would slow down to a year-on-year growth rate of 0.5% in August, with communication equipment purchases and spending on recreation still on a downward trajectory.
June retail sales fell 3% in annual terms, the third consecutive month of contraction.
Indonesia's August consumer confidence index rose for the first time since April, reaching 118.5, with car and motorbike sales growing 32.4% and 3.2% year-on-year, respectively.
Retail sales are one of the major indicators monitored by the market to gauge economic activity in Southeast Asia's largest economy.
